items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Sol was the baritone player and then later Cecil Payne came in. Ernie Henry and then later John Brown, Dave Burns, Miles was in the band, Fats Navarro.

ctx.x: Chi-chi — I think is thank you, isn’t it?

But you see what I’m saying though? And like if a kid sees something, and you show it to him, and he can do it slowly, and — oh, I see that. It’s simple. They call it the light bulb going on. And I always say this, like I’ve been kind of fortunate, because if I explain something to you this way and you don’t get it, I can explain it four, five, six different other ways, like I think I can, because I’ve been pretty fortunate I’ve been able to do that. Because I hate for someone to come to me for someone, and I’m…

items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Dave Burns was the trumpet player. You know. That -- that was the band.

ctx.x: And Dave Burns was the trumpet player. You know. That -- that was the band. Nice little band, too, man. Good little band and we played and then I sent for my family; they came over. You know, they. And then I'd be on the road and different things happen, you know. Time went by. And then had a boy. So I had a little -- I had -- I had a little boy and then later on, we had a little girl, all right? And things, you know, things were going along okay, but I guess maybe she was lonely for France, too.
Your wife was a French lady?
